timeline.title: An Ordinary Beginning
timeline.text:
Nobody noticed anything important happened.
That is usually how important things begin

timeline.title: Becoming Friends
timeline.text:
Kerala trip happened
Small talk quietly disappeared.
Inside jokes followed.
Somewhere in there, friendship settled in without asking permission.

timeline.title: The Chapters In Between
timeline.text: Exams, doubts, growing pains — and through all of it, the conversations kept finding their way back.

timeline.title: Online Friends
timeline.text: The world went quiet; the friendship didn't. Texting and the stubborn refusal to let a good thing gather dust.

timeline.title: The White Coat
timeline.text:
There comes a point where effort quietly becomes identity.
Watching you become a dentist never felt surprising.
It only felt like watching someone slowly arrive where they always belonged.

timeline.title: The Conversation That Changed Nothing... and Everything
timeline.text:
Some conversations don't end friendships.
They simply ask both people to see each other more clearly.
This was one of those.
It wasn't the easiest page in the story.
It might be one of the most important.
Not because of what was said.
But because of everything that remained afterwards.

timeline.title: The Permanent Collection
timeline.text: Still collecting. The museum's acquisition department reports no plans to stop.

memoryCards.text:
The first conversation wasn't memorable because of what we talked about.
It was memorable because neither of us realized we had just created the oldest exhibit in this museum.

Not better.
Not worse.
Just unmistakably yourself.
I don't remember the exact conversation anymore.
I remember the conclusion.

Friendships become real somewhere between using someone's actual name...
and almost never using it again.

There are jokes you remember.
Then there are moments where you only remember laughing.
Somehow those last longer

The funny thing about healthy friendships...\nis that they survive being wrong.
Repeatedly.
By both people.

Every birthday quietly became another bookmark.
Not because of presents.
Because another chapter had been added.

It looked like someone recommending a book.
Looking back...
it was someone quietly handing over another way of seeing the world.

gallery1.drawerNote:
You probably never noticed this about yourself...
When you're genuinely excited about something, your smile arrives before your words do.

walls.title: The Reader
walls.subtitle: Wall One
lines: Some people read books.
You collected them.
Some stayed on shelves.
Some lived on your bedside table.
Some became conversations that lasted much longer than the final chapter.
Every recommendation carried a tiny piece of you with it.
Looking back, I don't just remember the books.
I remember the person handing them to me.
walls.closing: Every book eventually ends.  The conversations they started rarely did.

walls.title: The Dancer & The Dentist
walls.subtitle: Wall Two
lines: One part of you learned precision.
Another part learned expression.
One wore a white coat.
The other stood beneath stage lights.
One learned how to calm nervous children.
The other somehow calmed an audience without saying a single word.
Most people only know one version of you.
I've been lucky enough to watch both.

walls.title: Tough Guy
walls.subtitle: Wall Three
lines: You have this habit of saying,
I'm fine.
I'll manage.
I don't need help.
Sometimes it's true.
Sometimes it's simply easier than explaining what you're carrying.
The funny thing is...
The people who love you have never believed those sentences as much as you hoped they would.
walls.closing: Strength isn't pretending nothing hurts.  It's continuing anyway.

walls.title: Quiet Consistency
walls.subtitle: Wall Four
lines: You never tried to impress people.
You simply kept showing up.
For books.
For dance.
For dentistry.
For friendships.
For the people you cared about.
Looking back...
That quiet consistency became one of the things I admired most about you.
walls.closing: People often mistake consistency for ordinary.  It never is.

mirrorLines: You notice more than you admit.
You care more than you say.
You carry more than you show.
You laugh harder than you expect to.
You remember tiny details everyone else forgets.
You're much braver than your inner voice gives you credit for.
You're one of the safest people I've ever known.

observations.text: You become visibly happier the moment someone mentions books.
You celebrate other people's successes with the same excitement you wish people celebrated yours.

You call yourself difficult.
I've only ever seen someone who cares deeply and trusts carefully.

You remember birthdays, little comments, favourite foods and random stories people told you months ago.
Then you act surprised when they say you have a good memory.

When something matters to you...
you become incredibly quiet before making a decision.

You disappear when life becomes overwhelming.
Not because you don't care.
Because you don't want anyone else carrying what you're carrying.
You apologise for things that never needed an apology.

Trust takes time with you.
But once someone earns it...
they'll never have to wonder where they stand.
You've never realised how many people smile simply because you walked into the room.

You think this museum is about memories.
It isn't.
It's about someone who quietly changed another person's life without ever trying to.

secretObservation.title: One More Thing.
secretObservation.text:
The most beautiful thing about kindness is that it rarely knows how important it has been.
I don't think you've ever fully realised how many ordinary days became better simply because you were part of them.
Maybe that's why this room exists.

evidence.title: Shelf A — Conversations Disguised As Books
evidence.caption: Books were never just recommendations.  They became discussions that lasted weeks.
evidence.context:
Every highlighted sentence.
Every "you have to read this."
Every disagreement about an ending.
Some friendships exchange gifts.
Ours exchanged entire worlds bound between two covers.

evidence.title: Shelf B — Ordinary Conversations
evidence.caption: Weak Memory.  Tough Guy.  It's my destiny.  Three phrases.  Thousands of memories.
evidence.context:
If someone read these chats from the beginning, they probably wouldn't understand why they're here.
That's because the important part isn't any single message.
It's that someone was always on the other side.

evidence.title: Shelf C — Voices That Stayed
evidence.caption: Press play. Old cassette animation included.
evidence.context:
Some were advice.
Some songs were sung.
Some were complete nonsense.
Some were sent because typing felt like too much work.
Every single one somehow made the day better.

evidence.title: Shelf D — Places That Remember Us
evidence.caption: Maps eventually become stories.
evidence.context:
The destinations were nice.
But the conversations during the journey usually became the part worth remembering.
Funny how roads disappear from memory while the people walking beside you don't.

evidence.title: Shelf E — Highly Debatable Opinions
evidence.caption: Strong opinions.  Very little compromise
evidence.context:
Ice Cream Paglu
Cheese Paglu
Spicy Paglu
Zonatello Paglu

evidence.title: Shelf F — The Arguments That Never Needed Winners
evidence.caption: Movies.  Music. Feminism.  Completely unnecessary topics.
evidence.context:
The strange thing about healthy disagreements is that they rarely change anyone's opinion.
They simply make the conversation more interesting.
Some of my favourite memories started with,
No, you're completely wrong...

gallery3.glassCaseDescription:
Every museum keeps one display empty.
Not because there's nothing to place inside.
Because some memories are too personal to become exhibits.
The curator knows what belongs here.
So does the visitor.

gallery4.roomTitle: The Dance Studio of Her Story
gallery4.roomSubtitle: Some people collect medals. Some collect recordings. I collected the moments where you looked the happiest.
gallery4.wallHint: open a frame · the projector still works
gallery4.centerpieceText:
There are very few things in life that let us meet the truest version of ourselves.
For some people it's painting.
For others it's writing.
For you...
it has always been dance.
Not because you wanted attention.
Not because of the applause.
But because for those few minutes,
nothing else seemed to exist.
No exams.
No responsibilities.
No expectations.
Just music.
Movement.
And a smile that never needed to be forced.
That's the version of you this room was built to remember.
gallery4.reservedChairQuote: Some stories are written with words. Yours was often written with movement.
gallery4.reservedChairRight: Reserved for the Audience of One

performances.title: Blurry but beautiful
performances.description:
No stage.
No audience.
Just enough room between the furniture.
Turns out passion doesn't really care where it's performed.
performances.memory:
Some performances exist because people are watching.
Some exist because the dancer simply couldn't imagine not dancing.
performances.curatorNote: Archived from memory. The recording is imperfect; the moment was not.

performances.title: The Smile That Always Returned
performances.description:
Different costumes.
Different stages.
Different songs.
Years apart.
Yet every recording shared one familiar thing.
The moment the music began...
you smiled exactly the same way.
performances.memory:
It became impossible not to notice.
Dance wasn't simply something you enjoyed.
It was somewhere you belonged.

performances.title: Where Everything Else Became Quiet
performances.description:
Everyone has a place where life becomes quieter.
Some find it in mountains.
Some in books.
Some in prayer.
You seemed to find it between the first beat of a song
and the last step of a routine.
performances.memory:
Watching those videos,
I stopped paying attention to the choreography.
I started paying attention to your face.
It always looked lighter than it did anywhere else.
performances.curatorNote: The most honest recording in this collection.

performances.title: A Language Without Words
performances.description:
I've heard people describe dance as movement.
I don't think that's accurate.
Movement is only what everyone else sees.
The real language is emotion.
And somehow,
without saying a single word,
you always looked completely understood.
performances.memory:
Even someone sitting miles away,
watching through a phone screen,
could tell
how much this meant to you.

performances.title: The Version Of You I Hope Never Changes
performances.description:
Life changes people.
Responsibilities grow.
Dreams become careers.
Time becomes harder to find.
I hope this part of you never disappears.
I hope there is always some song,
some empty room,
or some stage somewhere,
where you get to forget the rest of the world again.
performances.memory:
Not every beautiful thing needs an audience.
Some moments are beautiful simply because the person living them is happy.
performances.curatorNote: Filed under:  The happiest version of Chicko.

performances.title: Still Dancing
performances.description:
Museums usually preserve finished stories.
This isn't one of them.
Somewhere,
another rehearsal is happening.
Another performance is waiting.
Another recording will eventually find its way here.
This room was never meant to be completed.
Only continued.
performances.memory:
Some passions don't become smaller with time.
They simply become part of who someone is.

specialExhibits.label: First Performance
specialExhibits.note: Where the language was first spoken in public.

specialExhibits.label: Favorite Performance
specialExhibits.note: By unanimous vote of a jury of one.

specialExhibits.label: Most Emotional Performance
specialExhibits.note: Nobody remembers the decorations. Everybody remembers the dance.

specialExhibits.label: The One She Doesn't Know I Saved
Every Performance Together
specialExhibits.note: A standing exhibit. It grows every year.

specialExhibits.label: Performances That Made Me Proud
specialExhibits.note: Curatorial note: all of them. This label is a formality.

studioCase.label: The Dance Shoes
studioCase.note: Every scratch tells the same story. Someone loved this enough to keep coming back.

studioCase.label: Backstage Pass
studioCase.note: Some people watched from the front row. I mostly watched from a phone screen. Turns out distance doesn't stop someone from noticing joy.

studioCase.label: Medals & Ribbons
studioCase.note: The medals celebrate the performance. The real achievement was finding something that made you this happy.

studioCase.label: Rehearsal Notebook
studioCase.note: The audience remembers the performance. The notebook remembers the work.

studioCase.label: Old Performance Programs
studioCase.note: Her name, printed small, in evenings that felt enormous.

studioCase.label: Music Cue Sheet
studioCase.note: Long after the song ends, the feeling somehow stays.

gallery4.hiddenNote: You never looked at the audience. You just danced.
gallery4.hiddenCompartmentNote: Behind the fourth frame, tucked into the ballet barre, there's a note. It says: "This studio was never really about the steps."
gallery4.hairpinNote: A forgotten hairpin, catalogued with full museum honours. Exhibit condition: bent. Sentimental value: priceless.
gallery4.scheduleNote: A folded performance schedule. Every entry circled. Someone never intended to miss a single one.

cassettes.label: Laugh
cassettes.why: If happiness had a sound, this would be one version of it.

cassettes.label: Advice
cassettes.why: Delivered reluctantly, worded perfectly, remembered for years.

cassettes.label: Random
cassettes.why: Four minutes. Subject: nothing. Importance: everything.

cassettes.label: Late Night
cassettes.why: The conversations that only exist after midnight, when honesty gets easier.

cassettes.label: Books
cassettes.why: Reviews, arguments, and at least one dramatic reading of a favourite paragraph.

songs.title: Track 01 — The Rainy Day Song
songs.why: Why it reminds me of you: it sounds exactly like the evenings we did nothing, and it was somehow the best part of the month.

songs.title: Track 02 — The Study Session Loop
songs.why: Where I first heard it: exam season. When I think of it: your occasional sigh over another page.

songs.title: Track 03 — The One Sent at Midnight
songs.why: No message. Just the link. Sometimes a song says the thing neither person knows how to.

songs.title: Track 04 — The Birthday Song (Off-Key Version)
songs.why: Performed annually, always terribly, always meant completely.

gallery5.silenceBoothLabel: Some of our best conversations weren't filled with words.
gallery5.laughExhibitLabel: If happiness had a sound, this would be one version of it.

thankYouNotes: Thank you for becoming one of the few people I never had to pretend around.,
Thank you for every conversation that started with absolutely nothing and somehow became the best part of my day.,
You made 'normal' feel special without ever trying.,
Thank you for trusting me a little more than you trusted most people. I know that wasn't easy.,
Thank you for every time you recommended a book knowing I'd probably end up loving it.,
You never realised it, but you made me look forward to ordinary days.,
Thank you for making me laugh in ways that still randomly come back to me months later.,
Every friendship has its own language. Ours somehow included books, 'Weak Memory,' 'Tough Guy,' and blaming destiny.,
Thank you for always caring more deeply than you let people see.,
I don't think you'll ever understand how comforting your presence has been in my life.,
Thank you for letting me celebrate your victories as if they were my own.,
Thank you for every random picture, every random update, every random thought you decided to share with me.,
You made distance feel smaller than it actually was.,
Thank you for every late-night conversation that quietly fixed a difficult day.,
Some people make memories through grand adventures. We somehow managed it through conversations.,
Thank you for making reading feel like something we shared instead of something we individually did.,
Thank you for always being honest, even when honesty would've been easier to avoid.,
I don't think I've ever told you enough how proud I am of the person you've become.,
Thank you for every time you believed I was capable of helping you.,
You somehow made caring for you feel effortless.,
Thank you for all the little updates that probably seemed insignificant to you but meant a lot to me.,
Somewhere along the way, you quietly became one of my favourite people.,
Thank you for every 'It's my destiny' that was followed by you getting back up and trying again anyway.,
You probably think you don't leave much of an impact on people. This museum exists as evidence that you do.,
More than anything else, thank you for simply staying.[
Thank you for showing me that strength isn't always loud. Sometimes it's simply choosing to continue when life keeps making things difficult.,
Thank you for every time you trusted me enough to tell me what was going on, even when your first instinct was to deal with it alone.,
You once told me that asking people for help doesn't come naturally to you. I hope one day accepting help feels just as natural as giving it.,
Thank you for letting me be one of the people who gets to worry about you.,
You have this habit of saying 'I'm fine' while carrying far more than anyone around you realizes.,
Thank you for never pretending to be perfect. You've always felt wonderfully human to me.,
Every time you called yourself difficult, I secretly wondered if you realized how easy you are to care about.,
Thank you for every 'Jii' that somehow managed to sound different depending on your mood.,
Some of my favourite memories with you don't have photographs. They only exist because I remember how they felt.,
Thank you for never making our friendship feel like something I had to earn every day.,
You have no idea how many random things remind me of you now—books, cafés, yellow glasses, dentistry, and even the word 'destiny.',
Thank you for teaching me that caring for someone can be quiet.,
You once said I played a supporting role in your life. I don't think you realized you quietly became one of the main chapters in mine.,
Thank you for every time you let me celebrate you, even if you felt you hadn't done anything worth celebrating.,
You make people feel heard. I hope someone always does the same for you.,
Thank you for trusting me enough to slowly lower your guard over the years.,
I don't think you realize how much courage it takes to keep trying after disappointment. I've watched you do it more than once.,
Thank you for every silly debate that somehow became a serious discussion five minutes later.,
You've accidentally taught me that consistency is one of the purest forms of affection.,
Thank you for every conversation that ended with both of us somehow feeling lighter than when it began.,
Even on days when you doubted yourself, I never doubted the kind of person you are.,
Thank you for letting me witness not just your confident side, but also the version of you that quietly worries about everything.,
If kindness could become a habit, yours would probably look exactly like remembering the little things about people.,
Thank you for giving me enough memories that I ended up writing an entire museum instead of just a birthday card.,
And finally… thank you for simply being Chicko. Nothing more was ever required.
envelopeText: You once asked me why I notice so many little things about you.
Because you've spent years quietly becoming one of the people I pay the most attention to.
And somewhere along the way, noticing stopped being something I tried to do.

cabinets.label: The Reader's Cabinet
cabinets.contents: Dog-eared pages ,Pencil annotations, Bookmarks ,Library cards ,Highlighted quotes
cabinets.explanation:
Some people read to finish books.
You read to meet people hidden inside them.
Every recommendation you made wasn't just a book.
It was an invitation into the way you think.

cabinets.label: The Dentist Cabinet
cabinets.contents: White coat ,Dental mirror, Tooth model, Gloves, Exam notes
cabinets.explanation:
This cabinet isn't here because you became a dentist.
It's here because I watched someone refuse to quit becoming one.

cabinets.label: Weak Memory Archive
cabinets.explanation:
Contrary to the nickname,
this museum exists because the archivist remembered far too much.
cabinets.extra: Maybe weak memory in general but remembers everything about you

cabinets.label: Tough Guy Collection
cabinets.explanation: Exhibit proving that intimidating people can also be incredibly soft.

cabinets.label: Trust Cabinet
cabinets.explanation: It cannot be opened at first. Keep exploring the museum.
cabinets.extra: "Some locks aren't meant to keep people out. They're meant to protect what's inside."

drawerNotes: You reread messages when someone matters.
You don't ask for help until you've already tried solving it yourself.
You say "I'm fine" differently every single time.
You always remember the emotional part of a story.
You pretend compliments don't affect you. They do.
You always carry more responsibility than people notice.
You become quieter, not louder, when life becomes difficult.

polaroids.caption: The Last Evening Before Bangalore
polaroids.back: We called it "See you later."  Neither of us knew how much we'd miss this.

polaroids.caption: The Favorite jhumkas
polaroids.back: Somehow these jhumkas became part of you.  I honestly can't imagine them on anyone else.

polaroids.caption: The Night That Became Morning
polaroids.back: Midnight roads. Loud songs.  A sunrise which never became visible

polaroids.caption: The Bangs Experiment
polaroids.back: We cut the bangs.  We laughed.  We questioned every life decision.

polaroids.caption: The Date That Wasn't
polaroids.back: Planned as a date. Became therapy instead. Somehow... still perfect.

polaroids.caption: Exactly Where You Belong
polaroids.back: My favorite photo of all time.

polaroids.caption: One More Adventure
polaroids.back: No big occasion.  Just another ordinary day that became a favourite memory.

polaroids.caption: Where It All Began
polaroids.back: Neither of us knew back then...  this was the first page of a beautiful friendship.

mapPins.memory: Funny how ordinary places become landmarks once enough memories happen there.
The bill, the photo, the conversation, what you ordered — all archived. The inside joke stays classified.
Books bought, recommendations exchanged, wallets harmed. We are no longer allowed to make eye contact with the bestseller table.
Routes traced between cities, each stop with its own photos and little stories. The best wrong turns in recorded history.

stars.memory: Weak Memory - Funny how a nickname can stop being a joke.  One day it quietly becomes a name that feels strangely like home.
Destiny - You kept saying it was destiny.  I kept thinking it was resilience wearing a disguise.
Birthday - Every birthday gave me another excuse to remind you how important you are.  This year... I accidentally built a museum.

The Courage to Trust - Trust was never something you gave away easily.  It arrived slowly.  Conversation after conversation.  Until one day I realised I wasn't standing outside the walls anymore.  I was simply... welcomed in.
The Reader - Every book you recommended carried a small piece of you with it.  Looking back, I wasn't only learning new stories.  I was slowly learning yours.

The Laugh That Stayed - I don't remember every joke.  I don't remember every punchline.  But I remember laughing so hard that for a little while, nothing else in the world mattered.  Funny how happiness remembers itself.

The Days Without a Reason - Some days you simply said,  "I don't know... I just don't feel okay."  You taught me that not every feeling needs an explanation.  Sometimes being there is a better answer than finding one.

Becoming - I watched someone slowly become the person she had been working towards for years.  It didn't happen overnight.  It happened through countless ordinary days that no one applauded.  Somehow, those became my favourite ones.

The Things You Never Notice - You have always thought people remember the big things.  I remembered the little ones.  The random updates.  The "Jii."  The books.  The conversations.  The way you quietly cared.

Distance - Different cities never really felt like different worlds.  Somehow,  conversations kept finding their way across the distance.  Some friendships measure themselves in kilometres.  Ours always measured itself in conversations.

Ordinary Days - If someone asked me which day was my favourite,  I honestly couldn't answer.  Because most of my favourite memories with you weren't extraordinary.  They were simply ordinary days spent with the right person.
The Museum - People usually build museums for history.  I built this one for gratitude.  Because one ordinary friendship somehow left behind enough memories to deserve its own wing.

gallery10.brightestStarText:
Every star in this room is a memory.
Every room in this museum is a thank you.
But if someone asked me what the greatest exhibit was...
It wouldn't be the books.
Or the photographs.
Or the conversations.
It would simply be this:
I had the privilege of knowing you.

letters.title: I Don't Think I Ever Properly Told You
body: There isn't one moment that explains why you're so important to me. That's probably why this museum exists instead of a single story., You became important through hundreds of ordinary conversations, random book recommendations, terrible jokes, long discussions, quiet days, birthdays, difficult days and all the moments that never looked important while they were happening., Somewhere along the way, you stopped becoming someone I knew and quietly became someone whose existence genuinely made my life better., I don't think I've ever properly said thank you for that., So here it is, written somewhere permanent.

letters.title: Watching You Become Yourself
body: One of my favourite things has been watching you slowly become the person you always wanted to be.,
Not because the journey was easy. I've seen enough to know it wasn't.,
I've watched you doubt yourself, question yourself, get frustrated, call things your destiny, pick yourself back up and continue anyway.,
I don't think you realise how inspiring that has been to watch.,
I hope one day you become as proud of yourself as I've quietly been of you.

letters.title: About The Person You Think You Are
body: Sometimes I listen to the way you describe yourself and wonder if we're talking about the same person.,
You notice your mistakes first. I notice how much you care.,
You notice where you fell short. I notice how many times you still tried.,
You notice everything you aren't yet. I notice the person you've already become.,
Maybe neither of us is completely right.,
But if one of us has to borrow the other's perspective for a while, I hope you'll borrow mine.

letters.title: The Trust You Never Announced
body: Trust doesn't usually arrive with an announcement.,
One day I just realised you had started telling me things you didn't always tell everyone else.,
You started letting me worry about you.,
You started asking me what I thought.,
Knowing how carefully you trust people, I don't think you'll ever understand how much that meant to me.,
Thank you for making room for me inside a part of your life that you've always protected carefully.

letters.title: On The Days You Don't Feel Okay
body: You've taught me that not every difficult day comes with a reason.,
Sometimes there isn't an explanation.,
Sometimes the only honest answer is, 'I don't know, I just don't feel okay today.',
I hope you never feel guilty for those days.,
You don't have to earn the right to be cared for by first explaining why you're hurting.,
On the days words become difficult, I hope you remember that someone is still happy to simply sit beside you.

letters.title: Why I Built This Place
body: At some point I realised that almost every important memory I had involving you looked completely ordinary.,
None of them seemed museum-worthy on their own.,
A random conversation.,
A book recommendation.,
A birthday.,
A joke.,
A difficult day.,
Someone else would've forgotten most of them.,
I couldn't.,
So I built a place where ordinary moments get treated like masterpieces.,
Because that's exactly what they became to me.

letters.title: To The Girl Who Thinks She Has To Handle Everything Alone
body: I've noticed something about you over the years.,
When life becomes difficult, your first instinct isn't to ask for help. It's to quietly convince yourself that you'll figure it out somehow.,
And most of the time, you do.,
But I hope you also remember that strength isn't measured by how much you can carry alone.,
Sometimes the strongest thing you can do is let someone else carry a little of the weight with you.,
You don't become less capable because someone helped you. You just become a little less tired.,
If this letter ever finds you on one of those heavy days, let it remind you of something simple:,
You were never expected to do everything by yourself.

letters.title: The Things I Hope Never Change
body: I know people change. I hope you do.,
I hope you become happier, more confident and more at peace with yourself every year.,
But there are a few things I secretly hope life never manages to take away from you.,
I hope you always get excited about discovering a good book.,
I hope you never lose the curiosity that makes you ask questions.,
I hope you keep caring as deeply as you do now, even though I know that sometimes makes life harder.,
I hope your laugh always arrives before you realise you're laughing.,
And I hope you never stop being the kind of person who unknowingly makes other people's lives better simply by being in them.

letters.title: If We Ever Drift Apart
body: Life has a strange habit of changing people's routines.,
Cities change.,
Jobs change.,
People become busy.,
Sometimes conversations become less frequent without anyone meaning for that to happen.,
If that ever happens to us, I hope you never mistake silence for absence.,
Some friendships don't disappear.,
They simply wait until both people find their way back to the conversation.,
No matter how much time passes, I don't think I'll ever look back at this chapter as anything other than one of the happiest parts of my life.

letters.title: Happy Birthday, Chicko
body: Birthdays usually come with gifts.,
This year, mine happens to look like a museum.,
Not because I wanted to impress you.,
Because somewhere along the way I realised I had collected far too many reasons to be grateful that you exist.,
Every room in this place is really saying the same thing in a hundred different ways.,
Thank you.,
Thank you for every ordinary moment that quietly became unforgettable.,
I hope this birthday reminds you of something that life sometimes makes us forget:,
You matter more than you realise.

letters.title: For Every Future Version Of You
body: I wonder what you'll be like when you read this years from now.,
Maybe you'll have achieved everything you're working towards.,
Maybe you'll still be figuring life out.,
Maybe you'll laugh at the version of yourself reading too late into the night.,
Maybe you'll still blame destiny whenever something goes wrong.,
Whatever changes, I hope one thing never does.,
I hope you're always kind to yourself.,
You've spent so much of your life encouraging other people.,
I hope one day you speak to yourself with that same kindness.

letters.title: Always
body: I spent a long time wondering how this museum should end.,
The truth is, I couldn't find a perfect ending.,
Because endings usually belong to finished stories.,
Ours isn't finished.,
There are still books to recommend.,
Still birthdays to celebrate.,
Still conversations that haven't happened yet.,
Still versions of both of us that haven't met each other.,
So instead of saying goodbye, I'll simply leave this here.,
Thank you for being one of the best chapters of my life.,
With love,,
Weak Memory

gallery11.hiddenLetterText: The rest of the story still hasn't been written.

gallery12.futureFrameLabel: Reserved for the version of you that neither of us has met yet.

corridorFrames: Some people become important all at once. You became important one ordinary conversation at a time.
Thank you for every memory. Especially the ones you never realized you were creating.
You never had to be extraordinary to become unforgettable.
One day you'll look back and realize that someone loved the ordinary version of you the most.
The best chapters are rarely the loudest ones.
Every room behind you was simply another way of saying...Thank you.
Happy Birthday, Chicko. Thank you for being one of the best chapters of my life.
epilogueLines: Every museum tells the story of something that mattered.
This one preserved something much smaller.
Nothing inside these walls changed the world.
But every room quietly changed mine.
postCreditsLetter: Thank you for taking the time to walk through all these rooms.
I know this is probably one of the strangest birthday gifts you've ever received.
I accidentally built an entire museum.
Not because I wanted to make something grand.
But because somewhere along the way I realized I had collected far too many memories to fit inside a simple birthday message.
Every room you walked through was really trying to say the same thing.
Every difficult day you trusted me with.
Every version of yourself that allowed me to know you.
If there's one thing I hope you take away from all of this, it isn't that I remember a lot.
You once told me that you push people away.
That asking for help doesn't come naturally.
Maybe all of that is true.
But this museum is proof of something else.
And someone thought that even your ordinary days deserved to be displayed like works of art.
So whenever life convinces you that you aren't enough...
I hope you remember this place.
there is an entire museum that exists for one reason.

birdFacts: The mirror in Gallery Two isn't an ordinary mirror.
There's a locked box in the Little Things Room. Keep walking.
The brightest star waits until you've seen every room.
Some stories are hidden on purpose.
I am the guide. Not the exhibit.

rules: Some exhibits become clearer after you've seen another room.
If something makes you smile, stay with it for a while.
If something makes you emotional, that's okay too.
The exit is at the end.
dearChickoLetter: Dear Chicko,
Before you go any further, there's something I should probably explain.
Museums are usually built around extraordinary things.
Historic discoveries.
Great achievements.
Moments the whole world remembers.
This one isn't.
Nothing in these rooms changed history.
Most of these moments wouldn't even look important to anyone else.
A random conversation.
A book recommendation.
A badly timed joke.
A birthday.
A dance performance.
A quiet evening.
A message asking if the other person had reached home.
On their own, they're almost forgettable.
But that's the strange thing about friendships.
The moments that change us are rarely the dramatic ones.
They're usually the ones we never think to write down.
Somewhere over the last 15 years, without either of us noticing, those ordinary moments quietly became a collection.
This museum is simply where I've kept them.
Not because I was afraid of forgetting.
But because I wanted you to know how they looked from where I was standing.
You'll probably recognize some exhibits immediately.
Some you'll laugh at.
Some you'll completely forget ever happened.
A few might surprise you because you never realized I remembered them at all.
And that's okay.
Museums aren't meant to tell people who they are.
They're simply another way of looking.
So don't rush.
Open drawers.
Read the little notes.
Stand in front of the exhibits for longer than you think you need to.
Some of the smallest ones took the longest to build.
Happy Birthday, Chicko.
And Welcome.
museum.welcomeSubtitle: A quiet collection of moments, conversations, books, laughter, little victories, and the countless ordinary things that slowly became unforgettable because they happened with you.
museum.welcomeTagline: Walk slowly.  Nothing in this museum happened all at once.
